solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Act for each model

parts.note: per is Latin-derived for 'for each', as in 'per person'
a form is a pattern or model to follow

explanation.surface: An actor is cast for every model in a show, one part each.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on stage is to put on a show, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Page with a notice in about procession

indicators.note: in places the advert word inside the word for about

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A page boy and a printed announcement concerning a march.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is an organised march, a synonym for a procession.

clue.text: Maiden after doctor, a part in pantomime?

indicators.note: after says the maiden letter follows the word for doctor

parts.note: to doctor or rig something is to tamper with it
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A girl takes a role after a doctor in a Christmas pantomime show.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show; here it means a long, absurd palaver, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a pantomime is a farcical carry-on, a long confusing procedure or fuss.

clue.text: Frequently showing temper, blowing top

indicators.note: blowing one's top loses the head, so the first letter of the temper word goes

parts.note: to temper is to moderate or soften

explanation.surface: Someone often loses their temper and blows their top.
explanation.definitionFit: Two adverbs meaning many times or repeatedly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lost in thought? Not even close

definitions.meaning: a long distance off, far wide of the mark

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both distracted and literally far away.

clue.text: What could make friend charge?

indicators.note: could make says the pal word is built round the joining word, its two halves on either side

parts.note: a mate is a friend
the question word stands for the connective and, the word that joins M to ATE

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what could turn a friend into an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: A whimsical clue: read the answer as 'M and ATE', and those two pieces could make the word for friend. The blog parses it the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official charge or commission to carry out a task.

clue.text: Without source of heat, I'm upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: the sun is our main source of heat
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed at having no heating.
explanation.definitionFit: Minus as a preposition means lacking, as in 'minus his coat'.

clue.text: Unimportant load being processed

indicators.note: processed means worked on and changed, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trivial consignment is going through the system.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means of little consequence, nothing to worry about.

clue.text: Saw a head of dynasty decline

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: to age is to decline or grow old

explanation.surface: Someone watched the founder of a royal line grow feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of 'see' but is the noun meaning a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, a synonym for a maxim.

clue.text: Fly in record time across border

indicators.note: across means spanning, so record and time stretch either side of the border word

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time
a hem is a border on cloth

explanation.surface: An insect sets a record time flying across a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera is the genus of mayflies, short-lived insects, so a kind of fly.

clue.text: Absolute shock when female fired

indicators.note: fired means sacked, so the letter for the woman is dismissed from the word for shock

parts.note: a fright is a sudden shock

explanation.surface: Sacking a woman caused utter outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' removes F (female) from FRIGHT. In British speech 'a right mess' means an absolute mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage: 'right' as an intensifier means complete or utter, as in 'a right fool'.

clue.text: Began struggling in lake in a city near Los Angeles

indicators.note: in places the struggling letters within the word for lake

parts.note: loch is the Scottish word for a lake

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of began writhing into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone began to flounder while swimming in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' jumbles the first word to NGBEA, and 'in' splits the Scottish lake word so that jumble sits between its O and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal Californian port city just south of Los Angeles, part of its metropolitan area.

clue.text: Is doing as ordered with what's given by doctor?

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient asks whether following orders is what the doctor prescribed.
explanation.definitionFit: A physician identifies the illness and pronounces their verdict on it to the patient.

clue.text: Shine in most of valley, in the morning

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter of the valley word is kept

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland
AM, ante meridiem, marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: Sunlight glints across most of a valley in the early hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief flash or glint of light, a synonym for a shine.

clue.text: Porcelain in magnificent store crew smashed

parts.note: royal can mean splendid or magnificent, fit for a king

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters of the two words are reassembled

explanation.surface: A shop's crew breaks some splendid china in the store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' turns STORE CREW into WORCESTER, an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous English china brand made in the city of Worcester since the eighteenth century.

clue.text: A plucky follower, gutted over knight and legendary king

parts.note: game means brave or plucky

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, so the middle letter of the follower word goes

parts.note: a man is a follower or servant
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A brave servant, disembowelled, serves a knight and a mythical monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' takes the A out of MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek king who led the army against Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Put back in check, say

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone is told to restore a check mark, as a request.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone or something to a former position, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Bomber in Trier, sort to be taken out?

indicators.note: taken out suggests destroyed or scattered, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bomber in the German city of Trier, some kind meant to be eliminated.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomber in the sense of someone who plants bombs for political ends.

clue.text: Fired up in fight, produces knife

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for fight

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scrap

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: lit means fired or set alight

explanation.surface: Someone fired up in a brawl pulls out a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for fired to make TIL; in a down clue 'up' means read from the bottom. 'in' places it inside the hyphenated word for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a narrow blade, a kind of knife.

clue.text: Unexpected hill trek delays film

indicators.note: unexpected suggests things turning out differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unforeseen trek up a hill holds up a film shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1955 Ealing comedy about a gang of crooks lodging with an old woman, remade in 2004.

clue.text: Nothing in measuring device can show shooting star

indicators.note: in places the zero letter inside the device word

parts.note: a meter is a measuring instrument
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gauge reading zero can still reveal a falling star.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is the streak of light from space debris burning in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Permission to pull out

definitions.meaning: ... as a noun is permission, as in 'by your ...'

explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as both a noun for consent and a verb for departing.

clue.text: Biting cold in desert

indicators.note: in places the cold letter within the desert word

parts.note: arid describes desert land, dry
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A sharp chill in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and pungent, as a biting smell or remark is.

clue.text: Fool taken in by phoney Creole dish

indicators.note: taken in by says the fool word sits inside the rearranged letters
phoney means false, so the letters of creole are faked into a new order

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A gullible person is duped by a fake Creole meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phoney' rearranges the cuisine word to CEROLE; 'taken in by' means the fool sits inside that jumble, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a slow-cooked stew and the dish it is cooked and served in.

clue.text: Burst ulcer causing suffering

indicators.note: burst means broken open, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A ruptured ulcer brings pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel describes deliberately inflicting pain or distress on others.

clue.text: Hunting dog ignoring black bird

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the letter for black from the dog word

parts.note: a beagle is a hound used in hunting hares
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hunting hound pays no heed to a blackbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Spider coming from altar — aunt going giddy

indicators.note: going giddy means spinning dizzily, so the letters are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: A spider crawls off the church altar and Auntie feels faint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Grouse, good and ready

parts.note: fruit that is ripe is ready to eat

explanation.surface: A game bird is in fine condition and ready for the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the game bird but is the verb or noun meaning complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse and to gripe both mean to grumble or complain.

clue.text: Second, perhaps, has spoken about row

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the spoken word goes round the noise word

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
a din is a loud noise, a row

explanation.surface: Someone talks a second time about an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinal numbers give position in a series, and second is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Level course, almost, for Badminton competitor?

parts.note: even means flat or level

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the course word is dropped

parts.note: a term is a course or period of study

explanation.surface: A shuttlecock player finds an almost flat course.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton is not the racket game here: Badminton Horse Trials is a famous English equestrian event in Gloucestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider in three-day horse trials, such as those held at Badminton, is called by this name.
